item.title: China commemorates 81st anniversary of victory against Japanese aggression
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-04
BEIJING, Sept. 3 (Xinhua) -- People across China held commemorative activities on Thursday to mark the 81st anniversary of the victory in the Chinese People's War of Resistance Against Japanese Aggression and the World Anti-Fascist War. The Chinese People's War of Resistance Against Japanese Aggression (1931-1945) was the first to break out and lasted the longest in the World Anti-Fascist War. Over 14 years, some 35 million Chinese were killed or wounded. Japan officially surrendered on Sept. 2, 1945, by signing the Instrument of Surrender. The war marked China's first complete victory against foreign aggression in modern times. Through immense sacrifice, the Chinese people made a major contribution to the salvation of human civilization and the defense of world peace. In 2014, China's national legislature designated Sept. 3 as Victory Day of its War of Resistance. Last year, China held grand commemorative events in Beijing on Sept. 3 to mark the 80th anniversary of the victory, including a military parade in Tian'anmen Square. On Thursday, a symposium was held in Beijing to commemorate the 81st anniversary. Li Shulei, a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and head of the Publicity Department of the CPC Central Committee, attended the event. About 200 people took part in the symposium, including veterans of the war, relatives of wartime commanders and fallen soldiers, and international friends who contributed to China's victory, as well as representatives of their families. Officials, young military personnel, and student representatives spoke at the event, vowing to remember history, honor fallen heroes, cherish peace, and build a better future. In Harbin, capital of northeast China's Heilongjiang Province, a series of activities commemorating the hard-won victory 81 years ago was held at the Northeast China Revolutionary Martyrs' Memorial Hall. Representatives from government agencies, businesses, military units, schools and social organizations attended a memorial event and paid silent tribute to those who fell in the War of Resistance. They also visited an exhibition featuring wartime relics to learn more about the historical significance and contemporary relevance of the spirit of the Northeast Anti-Japanese United Army (NAJUA). For 14 years, the soldiers of NAJUA fought in extreme conditions, suffering severe food and clothing shortages while facing overwhelming enemy superiority. Yet they still inflicted heavy losses on Japanese forces, making an indelible contribution to the World Anti-Fascist War. "We commemorate the victory so that we do not forget history," said Tong Guobo, head of the memorial hall. "The NAJUA spirit -- of unwavering faith, deep patriotism, and dauntless courage -- has taken deep root in northeast China, inspiring generations to forge ahead." At the Memorial Hall of the Victims of the Nanjing Massacre by Japanese Invaders in east China's Jiangsu Province, people took part in poetry readings and historical reenactments, bringing to life the harrowing stories of that dark chapter for the audience. "Both my parents were survivors of the Nanjing Massacre, and we lost six family members to the Japanese forces in 1937," said Cao Yuli, who was participating in the event. "We should always remember the past and value the peace we enjoy today," said Zhang Xinjue, a student choir member during the commemorations. In east China's Shandong Province, more than 3,000 artifacts that bear witness to the Japanese atrocities are exhibited at a private museum in Pingyin County. Among them are military postcards and letters and soldiers' diaries, as well as photographs, combat maps, and other items such as swords, helmets, and gas masks. Han Guangyou, the 65-year-old curator of the museum, has spent more than four decades amassing these artifacts from across China. "These exhibits stand as undeniable proof of the war crimes committed by imperial Japan," he said. The museum now receives more than 20,000 visitors annually. Han is currently collaborating with several universities to catalog, digitize and research the collection. "These stark exhibits serve as a sobering reminder for young people to remember the lessons of history and strive to build a stronger China," Han said. "Today's world is far from peaceful," said Zhang Shaoduo, an associate researcher at Shanghai International Studies University. "These commemorative events remind people across the globe that a stronger China remains a pillar of world peace." Also on Thursday, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun urged Japanese right-wing forces to adhere to the path of peaceful development, in response to Japan's record-high defense budget request for the 2027 fiscal year. "Our solemn message to Japanese right-wing forces: the right way forward for Japan is to fulfill its international obligations, fully remove the pernicious influence of militarism, and keep to peaceful development," Guo told a regular press briefing in Beijing. ■

item.title: Innovation, lifestyle redraw global perceptions of China
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-03
BEIJING, Sept. 3 (Xinhua) -- For Victoria, a visitor from Denmark, her trip to China this summer proved eye-opening: the scenes she had seen on TikTok became vividly real and tangible. Inside a shopping mall in Shanghai, Victoria joined crowds gathered around a makeshift boxing ring outside Unitree Robotics' newly-opened experience store, the first outlet of its kind in Asia. Two humanoid robots in pink and red helmets sparred before onlookers, and she pulled out her phone to capture the moment. "I watched clips of these robots dancing online, but it's really cool to see them in person," Victoria said. She described China's rapid advances in artificial intelligence (AI) and robotics as something "revolutionary, new and exciting." She also recalled watching a humanoid robot brew a cup of tea. For her, these novel encounters are far more than entertaining novelties -- they are vivid proof that China's tech breakthroughs are stepping out of labs and factory floors and into the fabric of everyday life. The booming growth of China's robotics and embodied AI industry is fully showcased at the 2026 World Robot Conference (WRC), which recently concluded in Beijing. The event drew over 300 exhibitors from 26 countries and regions, showcasing more than 3,000 cutting-edge tech products and giving the world an up-close view of China's fast-evolving robotics sector. Xu Xiaolan, president of the Chinese Institute of Electronics, noted at the conference that China's embodied AI industry has entered a critical phase of large-scale commercial application, with relevant products transitioning from small-scale trial operation to widespread market deployment. China has developed more than 400 complete humanoid robot products, over half of the global total, data from China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology showed in July, while a WRC report revealed that China shipped more than 40,000 humanoid robots in the first half of 2026, accounting for 97 percent of global shipments. As China's tech sector, particularly the robotics industry, flourishes, global perceptions of the country's technological capabilities are changing profoundly. Back in 2008, Rebecca Fannin, author of "Silicon Dragon," predicted the rise of China's tech sector in her book, a forecast that was widely dismissed at the time. Today, the tide has turned. Fannin said global audiences increasingly recognize China as a leading innovative nation, as Chinese-made products ranging from humanoid robots and electric vehicles to intelligent robotic lawnmowers and smart laundry appliances gain growing traction in the United States and beyond. "We're looking to China as a leader of the futuristic vision -- that's a big change from the past," she shared in a program hosted by the National Committee on U.S.-China Relations, a non-profit dedicated to advancing bilateral understanding. Yuan Shaoyu, visiting assistant professor at New York University, shared his thoughts about China's tech rise during the program. "Many people now see Chinese companies producing products and platforms that are genuinely felt more innovative, more polished, and also affordable compared to the Western ones," he said, pointing to the sheer range of China's tech innovation. Technology is far from the only draw. Increasingly, Chinese culture and everyday lifestyles are also winning over young audiences in the West. From Los Angeles to London, Generation Z is embracing authentic Chinese lifestyle trends online, fueled by viral hashtags such as #BecomingChinese and #Chinamaxxing. A growing number of young Westerners now follow Chinese-inspired wellness routines: they wear cotton slippers at home, start their mornings with warm congee, and cut down on icy beverages to live healthier. Yet this fascination stretches far beyond health habits. Global young audiences are also drawn to China's streamlined, people-centered modern-life offerings, ranging from high-speed rail, friction-free online shopping and food delivery to hit Chinese TV dramas and original role-playing games. Eric Hovagim, an American YouTuber, thought China would be the last place he would visit, let alone settle down, because of how U.S. media portrayed the country. Many of his peers felt the same. Nevertheless, he encountered China and was shocked by what the country offers -- bustling metropolises on par with New York, only safer and more convenient, and a tranquil life in small towns no matter how remote. "We saw that and realized China is not a place we thought it was," Hovagim said. In Hovagim's eyes, international content creators and Chinese social media influencers play a critical role in bridging cultural divides and showing the real China to the world. By capturing everyday, unscripted moments of modern-day China, their videos build a well-rounded portrait of the country -- one that resonates with audiences across global social media platforms. China's recent visa-free policies have enabled more Western visitors to experience China firsthand. Official figures recorded 22.9 million inbound foreign arrivals in China during the first half of 2026, a 20.4-percent year-on-year increase. This surge of visitors reflects a broader shift in global attitudes toward China. A July Pew Research Center survey of 42,151 adults worldwide found that 25 out of 36 polled countries hold favorable views of the country. Separately, the 2026 Global Soft Power Index from London-based consultancy Brand Finance placed China second globally, with its score only 1.4 points lower than that of the United States. The result underscores China's growing cultural pull and international appeal. Captivated by the country's relaxing, fulfilling lifestyle, Hovagim hopes his parents will one day retire in Shanghai. He pictures them savoring its slow-paced joys: dancing alongside local seniors and pausing to sip warm goji berry tea from a thermos flask. ■

item.title: Across rivers and ridges -- China ensures school access for children
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-03
* In 2022, a 268-meter-high elevator and an aerial cable car system came into service, giving children from the deep mountains a "sky shuttle" to the clifftop school. A second elevator, rising 288 meters, opened at the end of July this year as visitor numbers grew. * Across China, governments are tailoring school transport to local needs, finding different ways to close the distance between home and school. * The efforts, backed by national policy, reflect a broader commitment -- ensuring that geography does not determine a child's access to education. KUNMING, Sept. 3 (Xinhua) -- At age 12, Lei Xin had already mastered a skill most adults would never attempt: navigating a treacherous cliffside trail in the dark -- not for adventure, but to go to school. For years, reaching school meant a three-hour trek for Lei and his peers from Nizhuhe Village in Xuanwei City, southwest China's Yunnan Province. The village sits at the bottom of the Nizhu River Grand Canyon near the border with Guizhou Province, while their school is perched more than 500 meters above them on the cliffs. Children used to leave home well before sunrise, often returning exhausted. For parents, the daily trek was a source of constant worry. Now, the most daunting stretch of the route Lei once took to school can be covered in just 57 seconds, with a new 288-meter-high cliffside elevator whisking students up the canyon wall at five meters per second. Lei's story is not unique. Across China's vast, often rugged frontier regions, millions of children face long, perilous journeys to school. From sheer cliffs to winding rivers, the obstacles vary, but so do the solutions. The efforts, backed by national policy, reflect a broader commitment -- ensuring that geography does not determine a child's access to education. CROSSING EVERY DIVIDE Guanzhai Primary School, perched on the cliffs above, serves children from surrounding mountain communities, including four in Nizhuhe Village. Cut off from the school above by sheer cliffs, the children had to follow a rudimentary trail carved into a rock face hundreds of meters high. Narrow and steep, strewn with loose gravel, the trail had sections barely half a meter wide. The steepest stretches required them to climb by hand. "Back then, I wasn't afraid my child would be tired. I was afraid something might happen to him on the way," said Zhao Suzhen, the mother of Lei, who had accompanied him along the treacherous trail countless times over the years. The change came with the development of the Nizhu River Grand Canyon scenic area. In 2022, a 268-meter-high elevator and an aerial cable car system came into service, giving children from the deep mountains a "sky shuttle" to the clifftop school. A second elevator, rising 288 meters, opened at the end of July this year as visitor numbers grew. Together, the two elevators can carry up to 1,200 passengers per hour, significantly boosting the scenic area's capacity while eliminating the congestion that once forced students to compete with tourists for rides during peak seasons. Now, the entire journey from the village to school takes about 30 minutes. Students take a shuttle bus to the foot of the cliff, ride an elevator, then continue by cable car to reach the school. On Aug. 30, as many primary and secondary schools across Yunnan welcomed students back for the new semester, Lei once again boarded his unusual ride. Stepping into the new elevator, he watched the numbers on the display tick upward. "The first elevator takes 90 seconds. This one, 33 seconds faster," he said, sharing his calculation. "I feel like an immortal carrying me through the sky." Free for local students and villagers, the "sky shuttle" also features dedicated student passages, with police officers and staff on hand during peak hours to keep the children safe. By the end of August, the service had safely carried nearly 1,000 student trips between the village and school. More than 500 km away from Puli Township, which administers Nizhuhe Village, another group of children in Yunnan began the school day on the water. At a ferry crossing in Banda Village of Bo'ai Town, located in a reservoir area, village official Liang Guoyou arrived early in the morning to help students board. One by one, the children stepped onto a ferry that carried them across the water. It's their version of a "school bus." The journey was not always this secure. "Years ago, privately operated ferries lacked unified standards, and safety was a constant concern," Liang said. Since 2021, local authorities have worked with schools, parents and transport officials to build a coordinated school transport system. Seven dedicated ferries now serve 12 crossings across the township for 329 primary and secondary school students and preschoolers. For 55-year-old ferryman Wei Jinlin, the difference could not be starker. "When I was young, getting to school meant walking nearly 20 kilometers to town," he said. "Now the children can take the ferry. It's much safer and far more convenient." According to local authorities, the ferry routes have safely carried students more than 147,000 times over the years, covering over 70,000 kilometers in total. Across China, governments are tailoring school transport to local needs, finding different ways to close the distance between home and school. In March, mountainous Chengkou County of southwest China's Chongqing Municipality launched a "Hope Line" school bus service, with 33 dedicated routes now in operation. The service uses fixed routes combined with flexible pickup points to tackle the "last mile" challenge for students living in scattered rural communities. In Panxi Town, Guizhou, authorities faced similar challenges reaching students scattered across remote areas and recently surveyed the travel needs of 121 students before launching three customized school bus routes. Four vehicles now connect eight villages, providing point-to-point service during school hours. BEYOND SCHOOL RIDES The impact, it turns out, goes far beyond the ride to school. Li Zhiguang, principal of Guanzhai Primary School, said that as the "sky shuttle" has made the journey less daunting and physically demanding, students become more cheerful, confident and engaged in school life. "They are more willing to speak up in class and eager to explore the wider world," Li added. They also have more time for the things they enjoy. "Now I can use those hours saved on the journey to read and exercise," said Wang Sichun, a third-grade student at the school, her voice bright. The benefits ripple outward. The "sky shuttle" has also enabled local co-development of education and rural revitalization. As the canyon's scenery and cliff elevators attracted more visitors, Zhao turned part of her home into a three-story guesthouse with 12 rooms. During peak season, bookings can be made weeks in advance. "Now I can look after my children while earning a living without leaving my hometown," she said. More villagers are following suit, opening guesthouses, selling local specialties or working as guides. Official data show that Puli Township now boasts 46 guesthouses and 159 specialty restaurants, with tourism supporting nearly 3,500 jobs. Cai Xiong, chairman of the company behind the elevator project, grew up in the mountains himself and watched generations of children make the arduous climb to school. "I know how difficult the journey can be," he said. "I hope the 'sky shuttle' can give them a safer way to school, so they can focus on their studies, pursue their dreams and one day give back to their hometown." Yang Bin, a professor at Yunnan Normal University who has long studied education development in western China, praised the local approach of repurposing cultural tourism infrastructure for public educational services. "This is not merely an improvement in transportation infrastructure. It is a safeguard of rural children's right to education, ensuring that frontier children truly have access to equitable and quality schooling," Yang said. He added that better educational conditions also support rural revitalization by helping to retain population and stabilize communities, providing a lasting social foundation for tourism and other industries. The efforts are now finding institutional backing. A national plan to build a strong country through education by 2035 calls for advancing high-quality, balanced compulsory education and greater integration of urban and rural education, while narrowing gaps among regions, schools and student groups. Earlier this year, China issued a plan to accelerate agricultural and rural modernization during the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030), calling for stronger basic public services in rural areas. It specifically requires more balanced compulsory education and better conditions for rural schools, including necessary small-scale village schools and kindergartens. Yang noted that these efforts can help address the longstanding challenges in rural education and narrow the urban-rural development gap. "The road to school is, in many ways, the first step toward educational equity," he said. ■ (Video reporters: Xiong Xuanang and Wang Anhaowei; Video editors: Yang Zeyi, Roger Lott, Zhao Xiaoqing and Wang Han)

item.title: Xi, Peng Liyuan visit Grand Egyptian Museum
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-03
Chinese President Xi Jinping and his wife Peng Liyuan, accompanied by Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi and his wife Entissar El-Sisi, tour the Grand Egyptian Museum in Giza, Egypt, Sept. 2, 2026. (Xinhua/Xie Huanchi) CAIRO, Sept. 2 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping and his wife, Peng Liyuan, visited on Wednesday the Grand Egyptian Museum accompanied by Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi and his wife. The two heads of state and their spouses took in the exquisite and imposing stone carvings and inscribed stone pillars. They then gazed out at the pyramids from the museum's observation deck. Entering the Tutankhamun exhibition hall, the two presidents viewed such prized treasures as the pharaoh's throne, the golden mask and royal chariots. Noting that China and Egypt are both ancient civilizations and countries rich in World Heritage sites, Xi said that across time and space, the two civilizations have been reaching out to each other, adding new chapters of everlasting friendship between the two peoples. Xi called on both sides to uphold the vision of civilization based on equality, mutual learning, dialogue and inclusiveness, and implement the Global Civilization Initiative. He also urged the two countries to promote the inclusive coexistence and mutual learning among different civilizations, and pool greater strength from civilizations to advance the building of a community with a shared future for humanity. Sisi thanked Xi for extending congratulations on the opening of the museum last year. He said the ancient Egyptian and Chinese civilizations share the qualities of openness, inclusiveness and harmonious coexistence amid diversity, which closely aligns with the vision of the Global Civilization Initiative proposed by Xi. The Egyptian side stands ready to work with China to step up people-to-people and cultural exchanges, promote mutual learning among civilizations, and make the world more harmonious and inclusive, Sisi said. ■

item.title: Xi leaves Egypt after state visit
item.description:

Chinese President Xi Jinping leaves Cairo after paying a state visit to Egypt, Sept. 2, 2026. (Xinhua/Xin Mengchen) CAIRO, Sept. 2 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping left Cairo on Wednesday after paying a state visit to Egypt. During the visit, Xi held talks with Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi. The two heads of state jointly witnessed the signing of multiple cooperation documents on Belt and Road cooperation, artificial intelligence, economic and trade, and industrial and supply chain cooperation. The two countries also issued a joint statement on further deepening their comprehensive strategic partnership. Accompanied by Sisi and his wife Entissar El-Sisi, Xi and his wife Peng Liyuan toured the Grand Egyptian Museum before departure. ■ Chinese President Xi Jinping leaves Cairo after paying a state visit to Egypt, Sept. 2, 2026. item.title: China's service trade posts steady expansion, as travel, transport lead export growth
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-03
BEIJING, Sept. 3 (Xinhua) -- China's trade in services maintained steady growth in the first seven months of 2026, as the export of travel and transport services drove more than half of the overall export expansion, official data showed Thursday. The country's services trade totaled nearly 4.45 trillion yuan (about 655.8 billion U.S. dollars) during the period, up 8.3 percent year on year, according to the Ministry of Commerce. During the period, services exports rose 17.1 percent year on year to over 1.77 trillion yuan. Services imports reached 2.67 trillion yuan, up 3.2 percent from a year earlier. The country's services trade deficit narrowed by 176.33 billion yuan from a year earlier to 900.25 billion yuan. A breakdown of the data showed travel and transport services emerged as the two export growth drivers. Travel services exports surged 27.7 percent, while transport services exports rose 27.1 percent. The two categories contributed 22.1 percent and 29.9 percent, respectively, to the overall growth of services exports. Knowledge-intensive services also remained a pillar of China's export mix. Trade in such services, which include telecommunications, information technology, finance, intellectual property and other business services, increased 6.6 percent to 1.96 trillion yuan, accounting for 44.1 percent of the country's total services trade. China has intensified policy efforts to boost service sector development. The outline of the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) and this year's government work report both made specific arrangements for this sector. In April, the State Council issued a guideline on advancing the expansion and quality upgrading of the sector. According to the guideline, China aims to make marked progress in high-quality service sector development by 2030, with the total scale of the sector exceeding 100 trillion yuan by then, while more competitive and influential "China services" brands will be cultivated. ■

item.title: Asia-Pacific Media Forum to be held in China's Guangdong
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-03
BEIJING, Sept. 3 (Xinhua) -- The Asia-Pacific Media Forum will open on Saturday in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, as the country hosts a series of events under the 2026 APEC "China Year." Multiple outcomes are expected to be unveiled at the forum, under the theme of "Building a Path to Shared Prosperity for the Asia-Pacific Community: Media Consensus and Action." Ahead of the event, participating guests are visiting cities in Guangdong, including Guangzhou, Foshan, Dongguan, Shenzhen, Zhuhai and Zhongshan. During the 2026 APEC "China Year," approximately 300 events are scheduled to take place across multiple cities in China. Notably, the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting will be held in Shenzhen in November. It will be China's third time hosting the event, following Shanghai in 2001 and Beijing in 2014. Adjacent to Hong Kong, Shenzhen was one of China's first special economic zones and has since evolved, over four decades, into a global hub for innovation and advanced manufacturing. In the first half of 2026, Shenzhen's trade with other APEC economies rose 33 percent to 1.98 trillion yuan (about 292 billion U.S. dollars), accounting for 68.8 percent of its total foreign trade. Experts believe Shenzhen illustrates how China's new growth drivers are generating new opportunities across the Asia-Pacific region. ■

item.title: Xi's four-point proposal offers Chinese solution for Mideast peace, stability: Chinese FM
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-03
BEIJING, Sept. 3 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping's four-point proposal on building a new security architecture in the Middle East once again offers a Chinese solution for achieving long-term peace and stability in the region, Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi has said. Wang, also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, made the remarks while briefing reporters on the conclusion of Xi's attendance at the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) Bishkek Summit and state visits to Kyrgyzstan and Egypt. Xi put forward the proposal in his talks with Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi, calling for unleashing internal drivers, advancing an integrated approach, cementing development foundation, and enhancing international coordination. International observers believe that Xi's proposal has offered a viable path toward resolving the Middle East's security dilemma, Wang said. During the visit, Xi had in-depth exchanges with leaders of various countries on world affairs and hotspot issues, speaking up for peace and standing up for justice, said Wang. On the sidelines of the Bishkek summit, Xi held separate meetings with Russian President Vladimir Putin, Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev and Mongolian President Ukhnaa Khurelsukh. Xi and Putin agreed to deepen China-Russia comprehensive strategic coordination, advance reform of global governance, promote a multipolar world, and jointly safeguard world peace, stability and development, Wang noted. Guided by Xi Jinping Thought on Diplomacy, China has been exploring a distinctly Chinese approach to resolving hotspot issues, Wang said, adding that no matter how complex the disputes or how intense the conflicts, China will always stand firmly on the side of peace and dialogue and on the right side of history. ■

(Xinhua/Yin Bogu) CAIRO, Sept. 2 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Wednesday called on China and Egypt to support each other, deepen cooperation, and continue advancing the building of a China-Egypt community with a shared future amid a turbulent international and regional landscape. Xi made the remarks during his talks with Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi, while emphasizing China's support for regional countries in building a new security architecture in the Middle East via upholding a vision of common, comprehensive, cooperative and sustainable security. ENHANCING BILATERAL EXCHANGES, COOPERATION Noting that Egypt was the first Arab and African nation to establish diplomatic ties with the People's Republic of China in 1956, Xi said that the older-generation leaders of the two countries led their peoples in striving side by side for national independence and against imperialism and colonialism, forging an unbreakable bond of friendship. Over the past seven decades, China-Egypt relations have weathered challenges and developed distinctive features of equality and mutual trust, friendship and mutual learning, solidarity and mutual support, as well as win-win cooperation, he said. Xi said the China-Egypt comprehensive strategic partnership has achieved leapfrog development in recent years under the guidance of the two heads of state. The two sides share similar views and have closely aligned strategies in pursuing development and revitalization, improving people's well-being, and upholding international fairness and justice, he added. Xi emphasized that China and Egypt should firmly support each other, maintain the momentum of high-level exchanges, enhance exchanges and cooperation in all fields and at all levels, and strengthen exchanges and mutual learning on governance experience. Xi said the two sides should promote mutually beneficial cooperation, better align their development strategies, tap the potential for cooperation in traditional fields such as infrastructure development, power, agriculture and communications technology, and foster new highlights of cooperation in green energy, electric vehicles, aerospace, the digital economy and modern agricultural technology. The two sides should promote people-to-people exchanges, comprehensively expand exchanges and cooperation in culture, education, science and technology, health, sports and other fields, and facilitate personnel exchanges and enhance people-to-people bonds, Xi said. The two sides should strengthen security cooperation, jointly combat transnational crime, deepen international cooperation in anti-corruption, firmly support each other's anti-terror efforts, and safeguard their common security, Xi said. The two sides should strengthen multilateral collaboration, further enhance coordination and cooperation on multilateral platforms such as the United Nations and the BRICS, jointly promote the development of the China-Arab States Cooperation Forum and the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation, jointly oppose unilateralism and acts of bullying, and promote a more just and equitable global governance system, Xi said. For his part, Sisi welcomed Xi's historic state visit to Egypt on the occasion of the 70th anniversary of diplomatic ties between the two countries. Sisi said that since the establishment of diplomatic relations, bilateral ties have developed in a sound and steady manner, and cooperation across various fields has yielded fruitful results. Egypt firmly adheres to the one-China principle and is committed to further advancing the Egypt-China comprehensive strategic partnership, Sisi added. Egypt is ready to work with China to deepen cooperation in trade and investment, manufacturing, infrastructure development, finance, science and technology, and new energy, strengthen military and security exchanges, and promote closer people-to-people exchanges, so as to benefit the two peoples and contribute to regional development and prosperity, Sisi said. Sisi said China, as a permanent member of the UN Security Council, plays an important and constructive role in international affairs. Egypt is ready to strengthen coordination with China at multilateral platforms, jointly address global challenges, and work together to uphold international fairness and justice, he added. The two heads of state jointly witnessed the signing of multiple cooperation documents on Belt and Road cooperation, artificial intelligence, economic and trade, and industrial and supply chain cooperation. The two sides also issued a joint statement on further deepening their comprehensive strategic partnership, and signed more than 20 cooperation documents covering such areas as digital economy, science and technology, education, and transportation. NEW REGIONAL SECURITY ARCHITECTURE In the talks, Xi raised a four-point proposal on building a new security architecture in the Middle East, saying that China supports countries in the region in developing good-neighborly and friendly relations. To promote common security in the region, Xi said that efforts should be made to foster the internal driving force for common security in the region. People in the Middle East should remain masters of their own affairs, and external interference should be rejected, Xi said, noting that China supports regional countries in strengthening dialogue on peace and security, exploring the building of a new security architecture for the Middle East, and taking their future into their own hands. Xi said that a comprehensive approach should be adopted to advance common security in the region and that given the multiple hotspots in the Middle East and their close interconnections, comprehensive solutions should be pursued. The Palestinian issue remains at the core of the Middle East question and should never be overlooked or marginalized, he added. The foundation for common security should be strengthened through development, Xi said, noting that lasting peace and stability in the Middle East fundamentally depend on development. China stands ready to work with Middle East countries to safeguard the security of international shipping lanes, advance development cooperation, promote the convergence of interests of regional countries, gradually enhance mutual trust, and eliminate the root causes of the conflict, he said. Xi urged that international coordination for common security in the region should be strengthened, and the UN Charter and international law should serve as the fundamental principles for handling Middle East affairs. The international community, especially external powers, should abandon double standards in the Middle East, respect the sovereignty and territorial integrity of regional countries, and safeguard regional peace and stability, Xi added. He also urged support for the United Nations' effective role in Middle East affairs. Sisi said that Egypt highly appreciates China's consistent, objective, and impartial stance on the Middle East question, noting that Egypt is committed to promoting de-escalation in the region, resolving conflicts and differences through political means, and advancing regional security and development. Egypt stands ready to continue strengthening coordination with China to ease tensions in the Middle East, safeguard regional stability, and explore a regional security architecture, Sisi said. ■ Chinese President Xi Jinping attends a welcome ceremony held by Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi prior to their talks in Cairo, Egypt, Sept. 2, 2026.
